questions.question: How does useState work and when should you use a functional update?
questions.title: useState and functional updates
questions.direct_answer: useState gives a component state value and a setter that schedules a re-render. Use the functional form, setCount(c => c + 1), when the next value depends on the previous value or multiple updates may be batched.

interviewer_intent.testing: React state model and batching behavior.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Expecting the state variable to change immediately after calling its setter.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Explain immutable updates and why state should not be mutated in place.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define useState and functional updates simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: State drives rendering
sections.content: Calling the setter queues an update. React then renders with the new snapshot; the current render's state value does not change mid-function.

sections.title: Safe increment
Remember
items: Never mutate objects or arrays in place.
Use functional updates for dependent changes.
Treat state as a snapshot for each render.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content: useState stores local component state and its setter schedules a render. I use functional updates whenever the next value depends on the previous one, and I create new object or array references so React can detect the change.

sections.title: Concept explained
sections.content: Walk through the example step by step, then say when this approach is a good fit and what you would test at the boundary.
